newsitem.title: USA: Pa. residents support property tax reform -- poll.
newsitem.headline: Pa. residents support property tax reform -- poll.

text.p: Nearly seven out of 10 Pennsylvania residents said they would support higher state taxes to pay for public schools if it meant lower property taxes, according to a poll released Friday.

The poll, commissioned by the business group Greater Philadelphia First, also found that 66 percent of respondents are in favor of increasing state aid to urban school districts so they can spend as much per student as suburban districts.
Support for that idea slipped slightly from 71 percent in a 1996 poll.
On other issues, the poll found residents by a six-to-one margin preferred paying for a state takeover of local courts through higher taxes rather than by cutting aid to local governments.

The poll found strong opposition to higher sales taxes as a method of financing regional infrastructure improvements. Only 13 percent of respondents said they strongly support that idea, compared to 38 percent who strongly oppose it.
Sixty-one percent said they would support Gov Tom Ridge's proposal to sell state liquor stores to private operators, while 28 percent said they would oppose the idea.
In New Jersey, 77 percent of respondents said they would support higher state taxes to pay for schools and other services if property taxes were reduced.
New Jersey beaches and the Camden Aquarium ranked high in support among respondents when asked what areas deserve continued state support, at 89 percent and 80 percent, respectively.
State funding for professional sports teams earned the endorsement of 35 percent, while the casino industry garnered an 18 percent share.

Greater Philadelphia First, an association of chief executives from 34 large corporations in the region, said the poll randomly surveyed 624 residents in Pennsylvania and New Jersey in November. The overall survey has a margin of error of plus or minus four percentage points.
